allowTimeBlockConflict.description: Escape hatch for the blocked-time check. Scheduling a task inside one of the user's time-block ("blocked time") ranges is refused and nothing is written. Set this true ONLY after you have told the user about the clash and they said to schedule it anyway. Never set it pre-emptively and never to silence the check. If YOU chose the time, move the task to a free slot instead.

assignees.description: Current shared-list member user IDs to assign. Call get_list_members first; omit to assign the creator.

board.description: Rough placement for a task with NO scheduleTime: "add it to today" means board:"today" and no scheduleTime. When you set scheduleTime, the DATE decides the column (today / this week / backlog); do not also send board, it is ignored in favour of the date.

deadlineReminders.description: Lead times to remind the user before the deadline (or "at_time" for the moment it hits). Up to 5. Only meaningful together with deadlineTime.

deadlineTime.description: When the task is DUE, completely independent of scheduleTime ("when I plan to do it"). Setting or changing this never moves the board and never touches scheduleTime or the Scheduled / Reminder only mode. Same wall-clock rule as scheduleTime: write it as the user's LOCAL time with no timezone suffix ("2026-08-15T17:00" for 5pm where they live), and call get_current_time first (freshly, not an earlier result) rather than deriving a date yourself. For a date with no time-of-day ("due Friday", "by the 15th") send that day's midnight ("2026-08-15T00:00") AND set deadlineTimeEnabled to false. Unlike scheduleTime, a date-only deadline resolves to the END of that local day (23:59:59), not midnight, because "due Friday" means by the end of Friday, not the first instant of it. Omitting deadlineTimeEnabled (or sending true) means the instant is taken literally.

deadlineTimeEnabled.description: false = date-only deadline (resolves to local end-of-day). Only meaningful together with deadlineTime; see its description.

listId.description: List ID to create the task in

matrixQuadrant.description: Explicit matrix placement. This is task metadata, never a tag. These ids do NOT carry their classic Eisenhower meanings: do = Do ASAP, meaning front of the queue today with no calendar slot. schedule = Do Later Today, meaning it stays on Today and gets a specific time slot later in the day. delegate = Do Mid Week, meaning it moves to This Week. It has nothing to do with delegating work to another person. drop = Leave Till End, meaning it moves to the bottom of Backlog. It does NOT delete or discard the task. Setting one also moves the task to the matching board column and reconciles its schedule, so do not send a conflicting board.

recurrence.description: Make this a recurring task. scheduleTime is REQUIRED with it and is the FIRST occurrence. Get the date from get_current_time (its upcomingDays list already pairs each weekday with its date) and never count days yourself: "push day every Monday" set up on a Friday means the NEXT Monday, and picking a date that is not actually that weekday is the single most common way this goes wrong. Say the weekday in rrule too (FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO) so the intent survives a wrong date. Sending recurrence without scheduleTime is rejected. The task itself becomes the recurring manager and Blitzit generates the occurrences from it, so do not create them yourself: for a 7-day split that is 7 recurring tasks, one per weekday, NOT one task per date.

rrule.description: RRULE string. Required for type=custom, and strongly recommended for type=weekly/monthly because it states the day explicitly: FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO for every Monday, FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=15 for the 15th. BYDAY is authoritative, so if it and scheduleTime disagree the rule wins and the anchor is moved onto the named day.

reminderOnly.description: Mode of the do-date (scheduleTime), the same choice the app offers as "Scheduled" vs "Reminder only". Omit it for the default, Scheduled: planned work the user will actually do (Blitz) at that time. A Scheduled task is anchored to its date: it moves to Today when due and stays in place. true = Reminder only: just a nudge at that moment, not a work block, e.g. "remind me to call mom at 6", "ping me to take my meds at 9", "nudge me Friday to check the invoice". It still notifies, but stays freely movable and its date is soft. Use true only when the user is asking to be reminded of something rather than planning to work on it. Needs a do-date (scheduleTime now, or one already on the task); not allowed on a time-block. Each returned task carries schedule.reminderOnly so you can tell the user which mode it is in.

scheduleTime.description: When to schedule the task. WRITE IT AS THE USER'S LOCAL WALL CLOCK with NO timezone suffix. "2026-08-15T15:00" means 3pm where the user lives, and the server applies their profile timezone. Do NOT convert to UTC and do NOT append "Z": that requires guessing their offset, which is exactly what puts tasks on the wrong day. (An explicit offset is still accepted when you genuinely have one.) Call get_current_time first: it returns the user's local "today" and "tomorrow" already resolved, so you never have to derive a date yourself. Call it again for THIS request even if you called it earlier in the session. A session can idle for hours between messages without anything showing that, so a relative time computed from an earlier answer, or from a time you previously stated, can land in the past. Set this ONLY when the user actually indicated timing: an explicit time ("at 5pm"), a part of day ("this evening", "tomorrow morning"), or something inherently a moment (meeting, call, appointment, deadline hour). "Today" and "this week" are BOARDS, not times: use the board field and omit this. For a day with no time-of-day ("tomorrow", "on Friday") send that day at midnight ("2026-08-15T00:00") with scheduleTimeEnabled false: a whole-day do-date with no clock time, overdue only once that day has ended. Only when the user actually means midnight ("at 12am", "at midnight") send T00:00 with scheduleTimeEnabled true. Never invent an hour.

scheduleTimeEnabled.description: false = whole-day do-date (no clock time; overdue only after the day ends). true = the exact time in scheduleTime, including a genuine 12 AM. Omitted, a midnight scheduleTime is read as a whole day. Only meaningful together with scheduleTime.

To reuse a tag returned by list_tasks/get_task, pass that complete tag object unchanged so its id and integration provenance remain stable. type.description:
Task type. Defaults to 'normal'. Use 'normal' for anything the user intends to DO, including work that happens at a fixed time (a study session, a focused block, writing a report at 3pm). A scheduled task is still a normal task.
'time-block' means the OPPOSITE: time the user is NOT available, reserved by something outside Blitzit (a meeting, a lecture, a commute, an appointment). It is not a unit of work. It is locked on the calendar, excluded from prioritization, and every later scheduling call is refused inside it, including the user's own. Only use it when the user is describing unavailability. Do NOT pick it merely because the user said "block", or because the task has a clock time. When used, it REQUIRES scheduleTime and estimatedMinutes (the block's duration).
